afp_interfaces.description: List of network interfaces (e.g., 'eth0', 'en0') on which AFP will listen. Use empty list to listen on all interfaces.

mimic_model.description: AFP server model identifier presented to clients (e.g., 'TimeCapsule6,108', 'Macmini7,1'). Affects macOS client UI behavior.

log_level.description: Comma-separated log level for default and subsystem logs (e.g., 'default:note', 'afp:warn', 'afp:debug').

log_file.description: Path to the log file for AFP server activity.

home_path.description: Path template for user home directories. '%U' is replaced with the username.

home_afp_flags.description: Default permissions (octal) for home directory creation: dperm for directories, fperm for files.

services.description: List of additional AFP volumes to expose. Each entry defines a shareable volume with its own options.

services[].name.description: Volume name (must be unique, no spaces). Appears in AFP browser.

services[].path.description: Filesystem path to the volume root.

services[].description.description: Optional human-readable description for documentation or UI.

services[].hidden.description: If true, the volume is hidden from AFP browser but still mountable by known path.

services[].readonly.description: If true, clients can only read from this volume.

services[].valid_users.description: List of usernames allowed to mount this volume. If empty, all authenticated users may access.

services[].allow.description: Legacy alias for 'valid users' (Netatalk 3+ uses 'valid users'; keep for compatibility if needed).

services[].hosts_allow.description: List of hostnames or CIDR subnets permitted to mount this volume (e.g., ['192.168.1.0/24', 'macbook.local']).

services[].file_perm.description: Octal file permission mask (e.g., '0644') for newly created files. Empty inherits from umask.

services[].directory_perm.description: Octal directory permission mask (e.g., '0755') for newly created directories. Empty inherits from umask.

services[].extended_attributes.description: Enable support for macOS extended attributes (required for Finder tags, resource forks, etc.).
